title: SymLift: Neural Semantic Lifting for Compile-Free Vulnerability Detection in Context-Incomplete Code Fragments
abstract: arXiv:2610.34431v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Missing project context can prevent build-dependent analyzers from constructing program relations required for vulnerability detection, while neural predictions alone do not establish auditable derivations. We present SymLift, a compile-free framework centered on Vulnerability-Oriented Neural Semantic Lifting for context-incomplete code fragments. A fine-tuned large language model reconstructs vulnerability-relevant control-flow, data-flow, memory, and resource relations in a constrained LLVM-like intermediate representation (IR), without reconstructing the full project context or directly predicting vulnerability labels. A deterministic parser validates the IR and maps its supported operations and relations into normalized evidence facts. Explicit Datalog rules derive findings with supporting facts and derivation traces, ensuring deterministic reasoning for fixed facts and rules. We evaluate SymLift on FormAI, Juliet, and MegaVul. translated_title: SymLift：面向上下文不完整代码片段的免编译漏洞检测神经语义提升方法
translated_abstract: 缺失的项目上下文会阻碍依赖构建的分析器构建漏洞检测所需的程序关系，而仅靠神经预测又无法建立可审计的推导过程。我们提出了SymLift，这是一个以面向漏洞的神经语义提升为核心的免编译框架，用于处理上下文不完整的代码片段。经过微调的大语言模型在一种受约束的类LLVM中间表示（IR）中重建与漏洞相关的控制流、数据流、内存和资源关系，而无需重建完整的项目上下文，也无需直接预测漏洞标签。确定性解析器验证该IR，并将其支持的操作和关系映射为规范化的证据事实。显式的Datalog规则推导出带有支持事实和推导踪迹的检测结果，确保在事实和规则固定的情况下推理具有确定性。我们在FormAI、Juliet和MegaVul数据集上评估了SymLift。Reduc（原文摘要至此处截断）
tldr: 提出SymLift框架，利用微调大语言模型将上下文不完整的代码片段提升为类LLVM中间表示中的漏洞相关程序关系，再通过Datalog规则实现无需编译整个项目、可审计且确定性的漏洞检测。
en_tdlr: SymLift employs a fine-tuned LLM to lift context-incomplete code fragments into vulnerability-relevant program relations in a constrained LLVM-like IR, enabling compile-free, deterministic, and auditable vulnerability detection through explicit Datalog rules.
